name: stri_match_all_regex
title: Extract Regex Pattern Matches, Together with Capture Groups

origin.description: Extract every regular-expression match and its capture groups.
origin.usage: stri_match_all_regex(str, pattern, omit_no_match = FALSE, cg_missing = NA_character_, ..., opts_regex = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Character vector of regular expressions. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: If TRUE, a string with no match contributes a matrix with no rows.

arguments.name: cg_missing
arguments.text: Text used for a group that did not participate. The default is NA.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: A list of regex settings, or NULL for the defaults.

origin.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Column 0 is the whole match. A group that did not participate is cg_missing. A miss fills that pattern's own columns with cg_missing, and extra columns beyond that pattern stay NA. A missing string stays NA. Named groups label the columns when pattern is a single pattern. The first column name is empty. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive. Each element is a matrix with that pattern's groups. A miss is one cg_missing row unless omit_no_match is TRUE. An empty pattern is a one-by-one NA matrix.
origin.example:
result <- stri_match_all_regex("a=b", "([a-z])=([a-z])")[[1]]
cat(paste0('stri_match_all_regex("a=b", "([a-z])=([a-z])") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Extract every regular-expression match and its capture groups.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Regular expression, missing value, or list of those. An empty pattern yields NA.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: If true, a string with no match contributes a matrix with no rows.

arguments.name: cg_missing
arguments.text: Text used for a group that did not participate. The default is NA.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: None, or a dict of only the regex settings that were supplied.

translation.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Column 0 is the whole match. A group that did not participate is cg_missing. A miss fills that pattern's own columns with cg_missing, and extra columns beyond that pattern stay NA. A missing string stays NA. Named groups label the columns when pattern is a single pattern. The first column name is empty. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive. Each element is a matrix with that pattern's groups. A miss is one cg_missing row unless omit_no_match is true. An empty pattern is a one-by-one NA matrix.
translation.value: A list of matrices, each a list of rows.
translation.example:
from stringi.regex import stri_match_all_regex
result = stri_match_all_regex("a=b", "([a-z])=([a-z])")[0][0]
print('stri_match_all_regex("a=b", "([a-z])=([a-z])") returns ' + ', '.join(result) + '.')
